Entegris (ENTG) Shares Skyrocket, What You Need To Know
What Happened?
Shares of semiconductor materials supplier Entegris (NASDAQ:ENTG) jumped 6.1% in the morning session after weaker-than-expected U.S. employment data cooled Treasury yields, easing interest rate pressure.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 in September, falling short of the 84,000 projected by economists polled by Dow Jones, while the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%. For the broader group, softer hiring eases interest-rate pressure on high-multiple growth equities by pulling borrowing costs lower. However, further deceleration in the labor market risks dampening cyclical end-market demand across industrial and automotive chip channels.Semiconductor valuations expand when falling yields reduce the discount rate on long-duration earnings, provided enterprise infrastructure spending does not deteriorate.
Is now the time to buy Entegris? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.
Entegris's shares are extremely volatile and have had 57 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 8 days ago when the stock dropped 3.5% on the news that benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose above 5.1%, renewing pressure on high-multiple technology valuations. In early trading, Micron Technology slipped 1.3%, Intel fell 1.3%, and Nvidia declined 0.5% on Nasdaq quote data.The pullback follows a six-session climb that had lifted the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index by 14% since the start of the week, according to Nasdaq index data. Bond yields reached their highest level since July 2007 after a stronger-than-expected September composite purchasing managers' index of 58.4 pushed the implied probability of an October Federal Reserve interest-rate hike to 73%, according to Fed funds futures reported by Reuters.Sector sentiment also faced cross-currents from competitor supply and investor positioning. Samsung announced it is allocating over half of its 4-nanometer foundry capacity to high-bandwidth memory base dies, raising concerns about future supply competition. Meanwhile, investor Michael Burry expanded short positions in Micron and semiconductor exchange-traded funds on expectations that memory shortages are cyclical rather than structural, CNBC reported.When benchmark bond yields rise, semiconductor valuations face mechanical headwinds because investors heavily discount cash flows projected years into the future. Paired with expanding foundry capacity and looming supply additions, higher capital costs make investors less willing to pay premium multiples for cyclical hardware makers until end-market demand visibility clears.
Entegris is up 86.5% since the beginning of the year, but at $167.05 per share, it is still trading 9.2% below its 52-week high of $184 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Entegris's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,390.

Domino Data Lab and EPAM Systems have formed a strategic partnership focused on helping pharmaceutical and life sciences companies move artificial intelligence projects from experimental environments into validated production. The collaboration combines Domino’s enterprise AI platform with EPAM’s engineering and life sciences expertise to help customers deploy GxP-validated AI models and governed analytics across research and development.
Life sciences companies are investing heavily in AI, but scaling projects across an enterprise can be difficult because of fragmented legacy systems, GxP revalidation requirements, and governance challenges. Domino provides the platform layer intended to bridge those gaps, while EPAM provides specialized engineering capabilities to integrate the technology into existing enterprise IT environments.
The companies will deploy dedicated engineering teams directly alongside customers to accelerate implementation timelines, modernize legacy code, and maintain compliance across heterogeneous technology environments. EPAM’s forward-deployed engineers will work alongside Domino’s engineering teams as part of the deployment model.
The partnership is designed to address AI use cases throughout the biopharma lifecycle, including drug discovery, target identification, statistical computing, and real-world evidence analysis.
For discovery and target identification, organizations can run AI agents, large language models, and machine learning pipelines against large-scale genomic datasets to improve candidate selection.
The companies also plan to help modernize statistical computing by providing biostatisticians and statistical programmers with a governed environment that brings together SAS, R, and Python, from analysis through tables, figures, and listings generation. Domino Data Lab And EPAM Partner To Accelerate AI Adoption In Life Sciences
Domino Data Lab and EPAM Systems have formed a strategic partnership focused on helping pharmaceutical and life sciences companies move artificial intelligence projects from experimental environments into validated production. The collaboration combines Domino’s enterprise AI platform with EPAM’s engineering and life sciences expertise to help customers deploy GxP-validated AI models and governed analytics across research and development.
Life sciences companies are investing heavily in AI, but scaling projects across an enterprise can be difficult because of fragmented legacy systems, GxP revalidation requirements, and governance challenges. Domino provides the platform layer intended to bridge those gaps, while EPAM provides specialized engineering capabilities to integrate the technology into existing enterprise IT environments.
The companies will deploy dedicated engineering teams directly alongside customers to accelerate implementation timelines, modernize legacy code, and maintain compliance across heterogeneous technology environments. EPAM’s forward-deployed engineers will work alongside Domino’s engineering teams as part of the deployment model.
The partnership is designed to address AI use cases throughout the biopharma lifecycle, including drug discovery, target identification, statistical computing, and real-world evidence analysis.
For discovery and target identification, organizations can run AI agents, large language models, and machine learning pipelines against large-scale genomic datasets to improve candidate selection.
The companies also plan to help modernize statistical computing by providing biostatisticians and statistical programmers with a governed environment that brings together SAS, R, and Python, from analysis through tables, figures, and listings generation. The goal is to help shorten regulatory submission timelines while maintaining required governance controls.
For real-world evidence initiatives, Domino and EPAM aim to help organizations standardize large and heterogeneous datasets through a secure analytics layer, potentially accelerating observational research across pharmaceutical organizations.
Domino Data Lab’s platform is designed to help enterprises build, scale, and govern AI applications, particularly in highly regulated industries. The company was founded in 2013 and is backed by investors including Sequoia Capital, Coatue Management, NVIDIA, NetApp, Snowflake, and UBS.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our strategic partnership with Domino marks a significant step toward AI-native transformation throughout the pharmaceutical industry, backed by EPAM’s forward-deployed engineering capabilities and industry experience across the life sciences value chain. With Domino, we aim to generate meaningful value worldwide using our AI/RUN Transformation frameworks in a complex, dynamic business and technology environment.”
Nir Kaldero, Chief Data and AI Strategist at EPAM
“Pharma’s AI opportunity doesn’t live in one function, and every team it touches has its own systems, timelines, and compliance requirements. EPAM and Domino are built for that complexity, helping organizations move AI into validated production no matter which team is building it.”
Greg Killian, Senior Vice President and Global Head of Life Sciences and Healthcare at EPAM
“Life sciences leaders don’t want AI that only works for one pilot. Pairing EPAM’s implementation experience with Domino’s platform lets leaders scale AI solutions enterprise-wide, not just within a single function.”
Ricky Mann, Chief Solutions Officer at Domino Data Lab

EPAM Announces Date for Third Quarter Earnings Release and Conference Call
NEWTOWN, Pa., Oct. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EPAM Systems, Inc. (NYSE: EPAM), a leading digital transformation services and product engineering company, will host a conference call at 8:00 a.m. ET, on Thursday, November 5, 2026, to discuss its third quarter 2026 financial results. A news release containing these results will be issued before the call.
The conference call will be live on the EPAM website at https://investors.epam.com.
Please visit the website at least 15 minutes before the call to register for the event. For those who cannot attend the live webcast, a replay will be available in the Investor Relations section of the website.
About EPAM Systems, Inc.
EPAM (NYSE:EPAM) is a global leader in AI transformation engineering and integrated consulting, serving Forbes Global 2000 companies and ambitious startups. With over thirty years of expertise in custom software, product and platform engineering, EPAM empowers organizations to become AI-Native enterprises, driving measurable value from innovation and digital investments. Recognized by industry benchmarks and leading analysts as a leader in AI, EPAM delivers globally while engaging locally, making the future real for clients, partners, and employees.
We are proud to be recognized by Forbes, Glassdoor, Newsweek, Time Magazine, Great Place to Work and kununu as a Most Loved Workplace around the world.
Learn more at www.epam.com and follow us on LinkedIn.
